title: Delegation status read silently clears a terminal child's queue without committing, so a later failed write cannot restore it
outcome: A status read (get_delegation) that detaches a terminal child and clears its queue either commits that change or leaves the queue intact, and a terminal follow-up whose later write fails restores the child's original queue in memory and on disk.
acceptance: get_delegation's terminal detach path accounts for a queue-only clear as a mutation (Detached.did_mutate or its equivalent), so memory and disk cannot diverge silently.
A terminal follow-up whose Phase 1 or Human-intake commit fails leaves the child's original queued prompts in memory and on disk, matching the pre-follow-up state.
A regression test drives a real child-row write failure after a terminal follow-up and asserts that the original queue is preserved, without weakening any existing assertion.
